course.title: Next js
course.description: A comprehensive modern Next.js course centered on the App Router and the skills required to build, secure, optimize, test, and deploy full-stack React applications. It progresses from project setup and file-system routing through Server and Client Components, data fetching, caching, Server Actions, Route Handlers, error handling, accessibility, authentication boundaries, advanced routing, performance, testing, and production deployment. It is appropriate for developers who already understand JavaScript and React and want strong practical Next.js competence.
prerequisites: Modern JavaScript fundamentals including promises and modules
React fundamentals including components, props, state, and hooks
learningOutcomes: Create and structure modern Next.js App Router applications.
Design nested, dynamic, grouped, parallel, and intercepted routes.
Choose Server and Client Component boundaries deliberately.
Fetch and mutate data on the server with appropriate validation and cache invalidation.
Build Route Handlers for HTTP integrations and webhooks.
Implement loading, error, not-found, metadata, accessibility, and navigation UX patterns.
Apply authentication, authorization, secret management, and request-trust principles.
Optimize client JavaScript, images, fonts, and production performance.
Test critical behavior with unit/integration and end-to-end strategies.
Prepare and validate a Next.js application for production deployment.

project.description: A realistic Next.js App Router study-planning application that combines routing, Server Components, Client Components, Server Actions, Route Handlers, validation, loading/error boundaries, metadata, accessibility, and production checks.
steps: Bootstrap an App Router project with current supported tooling.
Create the root layout and public home page.

Keep the dashboard page server-rendered while using a Server Action for mutation.
Validate form input on the server before persistence.
Revalidate the dashboard and redirect after a successful mutation.
Run lint, tests, production build, and production server checks.
project.explanation: The project keeps route rendering and data mutation on the server where possible, uses a small client boundary only for recoverable UI error behavior, and exposes a minimal health endpoint. The dashboard form demonstrates progressive enhancement through a Server Action, while revalidation and redirect establish the post-mutation navigation flow. The metadata and semantic HTML establish a production-oriented baseline; the final release checklist should add real persistence, authentication, authorization, and monitoring before a public deployment.
